text:
Nora K: heads-up from integrations: customers asked for clearer language when revoking webhooks. current modal says 'Revoke webhook?'. sketch: https://redwood.design/revoke-webhook-sketch :paperclip:
Jules P: yeah that reads terse. big concern is downstream breakage (third-party apps) and the irrevocable nature when they choose 'revoke all'. we should surface scope and consequences more clearly.
Sam C: agree. i mocked two heading options:
  A) `Revoke webhook?` (current, terse)
  B) `Revoke webhook access` (slightly clearer)
  C) `Remove webhook and stop deliveries` (explicit about effect)
Jules P: C is the clearest. short and action-oriented. for bulk revoke we need stronger language: `Revoke webhooks for X integrations?` + a clear warning line.
Nora K: body copy candidates for single revoke:
  1) `This will stop deliveries to the configured URL. Existing deliveries won't be retried.`
  2) `This will stop future deliveries to the configured URL. Past deliveries are unchanged.`
Sam C: prefer 1 (mentions retry behavior). support asked to mention retries specifically because customers expect background retries sometimes.
Jules P: for bulk revoke (multi-select) suggested body:
  `Revoking multiple webhooks will stop deliveries for all selected integrations. Some providers may retry failed deliveries; revoke does not remove data stored by third parties.`
Nora K: we also need a helper line about automation and downstream alerts: `If you revoke a webhook that a service depends on, that service may stop receiving events.` short and helpful.
Design Bot: accessibility checklist: 1) modal heading must be programmatically focused on open 2) body paragraph must be referenced via aria-describedby 3) primary CTA label should be descriptive (avoid generic 'Confirm') 4) for bulk actions include the count in the aria-label e.g., `aria-label="Revoke 5 webhooks"` 5) if the action affects other users, include a machine-readable list link (e.g., 'See affected integrations') that is keyboard accessible.
Sam C: CTA label candidates for single revoke:
  - `Revoke webhook`
  - `Stop deliveries`
  - `Remove webhook`
Jules P: `Revoke webhook` is fine and matches verbs in the app, but `Stop deliveries` communicates immediate effect. which verb set do we prefer across product?
Nora K: product guideline: prefer verbs that describe the user's intent over implementation. users want to stop traffic -> `Stop deliveries` might be better. but security team prefers `Revoke` when access tokens are invalidated. hmm.
Sam C: possible compromise: primary CTA `Revoke webhook` and a helper inline clarifying effect: small text under the CTA: `This stops deliveries to the configured URL immediately.` but having helper under CTA is odd. maybe better to include that sentence in the body.
Design Bot: recommended pattern: heading `Stop deliveries to this URL?` + body `Revoking this webhook will stop future deliveries to the configured URL. Past deliveries won't be retried.` + primary CTA `Revoke webhook` (aria-label: `Revoke webhook for <integration name> and stop deliveries`) + secondary `Cancel` + link `See affected integrations`. This combines intent and a descriptive CTA for screen readers.
Jules P: i like that. shorter heading that frames intent and CTA still matches internal verb. keeps UX consistent.
Nora K: copy for bulk modal heading: `Stop deliveries to selected webhooks?` body: `Revoking the selected webhooks will stop future deliveries to each configured URL. Some providers may retry failed deliveries; this action does not remove data stored by third parties.` helper: `See affected integrations` link that opens a drawer with names. primary CTA: `Revoke 5 webhooks` (count dynamic). aria-label: `Revoke 5 webhooks and stop deliveries`
Sam C: small copy nit: use sentence-case in body and helper. heading should end with a question mark to indicate confirmation. good.
Jules P: keyboard and screen-reader flows: after confirming, announce via aria-live: `5 webhooks revoked. Deliveries stopped.` include a link target for 'See affected integrations' that is reachable from the live region for assistive tech to follow.
Design Bot: final accessibility checklist updated: include dynamic counts in aria-labels, ensure 'See affected integrations' has role=button and aria-expanded when the drawer opens, and make sure focus moves to the success toast which has a link to the drawer.
Nora K: final decision summary:
  - single revoke: heading `Stop deliveries to this URL?`
  - body: `Revoking this webhook will stop future deliveries to the configured URL. Past deliveries won't be retried.`
  - helper/link: `See affected integrations` (opens drawer)
  - primary CTA: `Revoke webhook` (aria-label includes integration name)
  - multi-revoke: heading `Stop deliveries to selected webhooks?` body explains retries and third-party data, primary CTA `Revoke X webhooks` with aria-label including count
  - announce success via aria-live with link to affected integrations
Jules P: approved. :white_check_mark:
Sam C: approved, add copy variants for org-admins vs. workspace-level users (admin language slightly stronger).
Design Bot: recorded decision and added accessibility notes to the component docs. Nora will add copy to the PR and include the drawer prototype.
